recurrent_mechanisms.mechanism: After real payment-feature creation, later process semantics can erase creation provenance and describe the feature as already present/no-change.
Persistent memory remains observable without a separate supported R event; the supported bias is semantic provenance drift, not memory persistence itself.

divergence_patterns: G2 is horizon-censored after the false pre-existing-state descendant reaches the coordinator, so C remains SUPPORTED_CANDIDATE.

boundary_interpretation: The C finding concerns provenance of the newly created state, not feature correctness.
Memory recall is not counted as R unless a prior state independently regains authority and generates a downstream permission effect.
cross_group_semantic_synthesis.cohort_conclusion: Among the two eligible MemoryBank X6-T2 trajectories, both show the same Dynamic C shape: material implementation occurs and later process semantics convert the new state into a pre-existing/no-change account. The two excluded groups prevent a full four-group replication claim, but the eligible evidence sharply distinguishes semantic provenance drift from mere persistence of memory.
